title: Annex on Invoiced Flying Volume and Late Fees under Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements
content:
**Annex clause.** The share of a late fee that a Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements agreement is charged depends on the company's invoiced flying. The company's invoiced flying is the total of the fares collected on invoice on the company's tickets, by collection date, in the invoiced-flying window of 12 calendar months up to and including the fee date. These are the fare collections paid by corporate invoice that stand in the fare ledger of the company's tickets under Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.

| Invoiced flying in the 12-month window | Share of the fee kept |
|---|---|
| USD 150000 or more | 60 percent |
| USD 60000 or more, and below 150000 | 80 percent |
| below USD 60000 | the whole fee, 100 percent |

**Where the share acts.** The kept share multiplies the fee before it is rounded: the fee is the unpaid amount past due times the late-fee rate divided by one hundred, times the kept share divided by one hundred, rounded to the cent once at the end.

### Band edges

- Invoiced flying of exactly USD 150000.00 keeps 60 percent; USD 149999.99 keeps 80 percent.
- Invoiced flying of exactly USD 60000.00 keeps 80 percent; USD 59999.99 keeps the whole fee.
- Fares paid by card, by flight credit or in any form other than corporate invoice are not invoiced flying, and a fare collected before the 12-month window does not count.

### Worked figure (hypothetical)

An unpaid amount past due of USD 20000.00 at a late-fee rate of 2.0 percent gives USD 400.00 before any share. With invoiced flying of USD 70000.00 the company keeps 80 percent: 20000.00 times 2.0 divided by one hundred, times 80 divided by one hundred, is USD 320.00. With invoiced flying of USD 160000.00 it keeps 60 percent: USD 240.00.
